newsitem.title: USA: United Int'l's Asia unit to go public.
newsitem.headline: United Int'l's Asia unit to go public.

text.p: A subsidiary of Denver-based United International Holdings Inc said Tuesday it plans to go public with a global stock offering of class A common shares estimated to raise up to $100 million.

UIH Asia/Pacific Communications Inc (UAPC), which is developing multi-channel television services in Australia, New Zealand, the Philippines and Tahiti, said its unit, UIH Australia/Pacific Inc, also will sell $150 million in notes.
In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, UAPC said United International has also agreed to contribute $25 million in cash for additional UAPC common stock.

The company said it expects the money raised through the offerings and its parent's investment will be sufficient to complete construction of its facilities, cover anticipated start-up losses and provide part of the capital to finance new businesses as opportunities developed. It said it was pursuing TV ventures in India, China, Japan, Taiwan, Indonesia and Malaysia.

The offerings will be made through an underwriting group led by Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp. No initial offering price was stated. The company said it has applied to be quoted on the Nasdaq under the symbol UIHPA.
UAPC had assets of $344.96 million and total liabilities of $277.1 million as of September 30, the filing showed.

It operates in Australia through CTV Pty Ltd and STV Pty Ltd, in New Zealand through Saturn Communications Ltd, in the Philippines through a joint venture with Telemondial Holdings Inc, which does business under the name Sun Cable, and in Tahiti through UIH-SFCC Holdings LP, which owns Telefenua SA.
United International and its partners own multi-channel television systems in operation or under construction in 15 countries in Europe, Latin America and through UAPC, the Asia/Pacific region.

United International also owns a 50 percent interest in United and Philipps Communications BV, a joint venture with Philips Electronics NV that is the largest privately owned multi-channel television operator in Europe.
